title: Anne-Marie Duff in Sweet Charity at Donmar - review
transcript: welcome to one minute theater reviews I'm Paul so worse this is the Dhamma and I'm here to review Sweet Charity Sweet Charity with book by Neil Simon music by sy Coleman and Luke's by Dorothy fields which I saw at the Donmar & anne-marie Duff is perfect for the part she may not be as good a singer or dancer as those who've made a career out of musicals but she can sing and she can dance and she brings to the part all the emotional depth of a great actor you can feel her pain and you feel her ecstasy and to pick yourself up and try again smile is infectious charity is a taxi dancing in the 1960s in the kitchen and what that is punters can hire taxi dancers for a dance and sometimes for more than that now charity believes in love despite being conned and let down many times she remains an optimist and keeps looking for love when things go wrong she simply changes reality to suit her romantic view ironically despite being no virgin she remains an innocent which is the essence of her problem but it's also her strength you could simply dismiss her as a naive fool but instead her way of seeing the best in people and not losing hope is inspirational we wanted to find love even though we fear she won't Hassanein dance rendering of if my friends could see me now complete with the routine with a top hat and cane perfectly combos charities childlike unaffected miss I'm a brass band is a joyous expression of what it feels like to be in love but it's not a one-woman show Arthur Darvill as charities shy and secure boyfriend and Martin Marcus as a charming and charmed by charity film star are both excellent most of all there are the women who make up the rest of the taxi dancers their rendering a big spender is astonishing in the intimate setting of the Donmar where the audience is only four rows deep these women asking can I show you a good time is very personal the stunning choreography by Wayne McGregor reflecting the original work by Bob Fosse evokes cabaret and Chicago Robert Jones set to simple open stage but with silvery props and furniture reflects charities bright optimism in a harsh world what a way for director Josie Rourke to bow out as artistic director of domina I give Sweet Charity five stars
